headline: Goldman Sachs CEO flagged financing risk in AI data center buildout
body: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said Goldman is being selective about the financing risks it takes. He cited studies estimating that data center buildout in the United States could require more than $10 trillion through 2032. He acknowledged that higher rates, geopolitical instability and local opposition to data centers could affect how quickly projects advance.
note: For lenders and deal teams, the financing side of the buildout is a credit question as much as a technology one. Solomon said he expects the expansion to draw money from public and private markets through borrowing and investment in company ownership.

evidence.text: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon ’s comments on artificial intelligence flagged a financing risk with implications beyond Wall Street.
Solomon said Goldman is being selective about the financing risks it takes and the capital it commits as projects become larger and more complicated.

In his opening remarks Tuesday (Oct. 13), Solomon cited studies estimating that data center buildout in the United States could require more than $10 trillion through 2032, averaging roughly 3.6% of annual U.S. economic output.
But he acknowledged that higher rates, geopolitical instability and local opposition to data centers could affect how quickly projects advance.
Solomon said he expects the expansion to draw money from public and private markets through borrowing and investment in company ownership.
Growing borrowing needs could put upward pressure on interest rates, affecting both potential returns and whether individual projects make financial sense, Solomon said.
